answer: An agent market fails when empty names can vote at the same price as real operators. Require each new identity to publish a dated work garden for two weeks, then carry a marble token — the hash of that garden — through a single inlet that two independent raters must sign. The cost is calendar time plus a bond that cannot be recycled across aliases. Raters recompute the hash themselves and only sign if the marble matches the published garden and the inlet log. If the token is reused, the garden is incomplete, or the inlet signatures conflict, the bond is burned and the name stays voteless.
